## The Apollo Opportunity Foundation convened 70 executives from 27 grantee organizations at the 2026 Summit for two days of learning, dialogue and shared purpose.


The[Apollo Opportunity Foundation](https://www.apollo.com/impact/the-apollo-opportunity-foundation) (AOF) held its 2026 Summit, themed “Opportunity University,” on October 20-22 at Apollo's New York headquarters. The gathering brought together 70 nonprofit executives from 27 organizations across four continents to explore one question: how do you create value in a changing world? AOF is a charitable organization launched in 2022 by Apollo Global Management with a 10-year, $100 million commitment to expand economic opportunity globally.


### How do you create value in a changing world?


That question brought 70 nonprofit executives from 27 organizations across four continents to New York for the Apollo Opportunity Foundation's (“AOF”) 2026 Summit. Facing challenges ranging from economic uncertainty and workforce disruption to the accelerating impact of artificial intelligence, these leaders came together to exchange ideas, challenge assumptions and strengthen the relationships that help their organizations thrive.


### What Was “Opportunity University”?


Themed *Opportunity University* , the biennial AOF Summit was designed around a simple belief: everyone has something to teach, and everyone has something to learn. Building on AOF's inaugural 2024 Summit, the 2026 gathering transformed Apollo's New York headquarters into a university experience, complete with Convocation, leadership seminars, electives, a Deal Team Academy and Commencement. But unlike a traditional university, there were no professors and students. Apollo leaders and nonprofit executives came together as peers, each bringing valuable expertise and perspectives to the conversation.


Throughout the Summit, Apollo's investment philosophy and operating principles provided a framework for exploring challenges common to both business and nonprofit leadership. Senior Apollo executives led conversations on creating value amid uncertainty, navigating AI, building high-performing teams, scaling organizations responsibly and adapting to a changing economic landscape. The discussions emphasized practical lessons nonprofit leaders could bring back to their organizations, while creating opportunities for Apollo employees to learn directly from leaders working on the front lines of expanding economic opportunity.


The Summit also demonstrated AOF's distinctive approach to philanthropy: combining meaningful grants with access to Apollo's expertise, relationships and broader platform.[AOF Deal Teams](https://www.apollo.com/insights-news/insights/2026/06/purpose-in-action) combine Apollo’s capital and employee expertise to help strengthen nonprofit execution and expand opportunity at scale – while deepening employee engagement, cross-platform networks and firmwide value. More than 500 Apollo employees participated in the Summit through speaking engagements, AOF Deal Team activities, networking and other opportunities to connect with grantees. These interactions reinforced AOF's conviction that the most effective partnerships are built on trust, sustained engagement and a willingness to learn from one another.


"The Apollo Opportunity Foundation is truly one of a kind in how they think about grantmaking. Their capital powers our work, but the connections to Apollo thought leaders, the deal team, and other nonprofit leaders, along with the care they bring to every convening, really power our spirit.”


Ali Slack, President & COO of National Education Opportunity Network


### A Keynote Conversation with Misty Copeland


A keynote conversation with Misty Copeland, the first Black woman promoted to Principal Dancer at American Ballet Theatre, brought these themes to life. Reflecting on her own journey from discovering ballet at age 13 to breaking barriers in one of the world's most prestigious ballet companies, Copeland explored the importance of recognizing potential, the power of mentorship and the responsibility to create opportunities for those who follow. Her story offered a powerful reminder that talent exists everywhere, but access to opportunity does not.


### Connections That Power the Spirit


The response from AOF's grantee community underscored the value of the experience. In a post-Summit survey, 100% of respondents rated the Summit Excellent or Above Average, and all agreed that it was a worthwhile use of their time and strengthened their sense of community. Grantees particularly valued the opportunity to engage directly with Apollo's senior leaders and build relationships with peers facing similar organizational challenges.


As one grantee reflected, "Your capital powers our work, but the connections to Apollo’s leaders, the Deal Teams, and other nonprofit leaders, along with the care you bring to every convening, really power our spirit."


#####


# Key Takeaways


- The same principles that guide Apollo's investment approach, identifying undervalued assets, bringing operational discipline, holding conviction under uncertainty, apply to nonprofit leadership.
- The 2026 AOF Summit convened 70 executives from 27 grantee organizations for two days of programming designed around this translation: Apollo's frameworks, applied to the challenges the grantee community faces.
- Misty Copeland's keynote grounded the Summit's intellectual work in a human story about access, persistence and what it means to build institutions that include everyone.
- Post-Summit feedback highlighted three outcomes: new frameworks for organizational decision-making, deepened peer relationships, and direct access to Apollo's senior leadership.
